findings: Non-blocking (likely): expanding a source block after layout grows the card downward without a relayout. Cards can't be dragged now, so the overlap stays, and the snapped end segment can double back. Consider relayout on a significant measured-size change.
Non-blocking (confirmed): self-edges (recursion, calls within one class) are no longer rendered. Consider a self-loop indicator.
Possible: edges that run against partition order (callee to entry, unreferenced to type) rely on ELK accepting them, otherwise the no-partition fallback is used. Check with a recursive-main case.
